findings.note: A's turn-3 precombat main, empty stack, A priority. A owns Aegis Turtle (0/5) but B controls it. A has three Swamps, an Island and Murder; B has an Island and Unsummon.
Murder ({1}{B}{B} instant, 'Destroy target creature.') targets the Turtle and is paid with B from each Swamp. A's implied pass gives B priority with Murder on the stack.

B responds with Unsummon ({U}, 'Return target creature to its owner's hand.') targeting the Turtle and paid from B's Island. Unsummon resolves first and returns the Turtle to its owner A's hand. The card in hand is a new object (400.7), so when Murder tries to resolve its only target is illegal: Murder doesn't resolve and goes to A's graveyard. Unsummon is in B's graveyard and A receives priority. Four implied passes.
With the stack empty in its main phase, A casts the Turtle ({U}) with its Island. After two implied passes it enters under A, its caster. Nothing else changes and A receives priority.
